messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Security pager (INC-214512): multiple auth failures followed by sudden acceptances for service token `svc-infer-prx`. Spike detected 2026-03-15T14:20:56Z -> 14:28:40Z. See detection summary: https://pager.redwood.internal/inc/214512 and evidence index s3://sec-logs/inc-214512/index.json
ria: I'm on it. tagging @alex (security oncall) and @kyle (runtime). Quick ask: are we seeing request payloads with customer content or just auth chatter?
alex: initial grep shows mostly 401->200 sequences and lots of header fields like `x-req-id` repeating. There's a handful of requests with debug-level logs in body that include stack traces. Saving samples to secure bucket.
kyle: runtime looking. I'm going to throttle the proxy route and enable a short-lived denylist for the top 500 offending IPs. We'll also flip auth to strict mode (no token reuse) for a minute.
nina: CS/ops: pulling customer call counts. Early flag on three tenants (Morpho, Skylark, MediData). I'll create a priority list. Adding product-bot to notify product incident channel.
product-bot: Noted. Raising incident banner on status.redwood.com (internal only for now).
ria: containment plan (short): 1) disable token re-use window 2) rotate svc token 3) apply IP denylist 4) snapshot logs & storage 5) notify legal/comp. Who owns rotation? @harper?
harper: I can do rotation. Plan: generate new key in Vault, deploy to a single canary pod, smoke, then roll. I'll also add an immediate revocation timestamp to the old token. ETA 12m.
alex: evidence collection: pulling full raw logs and auth headers; preserving S3 object versions. Command used:
```bash
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket redwood-prod-logs --prefix inference-proxy/2026-03-15/ | jq '.' > /tmp/incs/214512/versions.json
```
alex: copied artifacts to s3://sec-evidence/inc-214512/ and wrote a GPG-signed manifest.
kyle: applied temporary runtime throttle (50% of normal) to route `infer.v1` at 14:24:10Z. Observed immediate drop in anomalous attempts.
nina: CS note: MediData is regulated (HIPAA), flagged as P0 for comms. CCing legal.
ria: legal already paged. Also asking SRE to fork a live trace for any requests that had a body to check for PII.
ina: customer impact snapshot: ~0.6% of inference requests across platform were affected during window; for flagged tenants the hit is higher (3-7% depending on tenant). Will prepare a customer-safe statement pending legal.
harper: new token created in Vault and canary deployed to `infer-proxy-canary` at 14:30:05Z. Smoke tests OK (latency within SLO, auth passing). Rolling to prod now.
harper: revoking old token at 14:33:59Z. Auth logs show declines for old token immediately.
ria: runtime change: disabled prefix caching for `infer-proxy` at 14:35:12Z to avoid replaying cached outputs.
alex: found two log entries that contain truncated customer identifiers in stack traces; no full PII visible. Marking as sensitive and running deeper string scan across recent dumps.
kyle: also discovered a deploy artifact in a staging bucket referencing `svc-infer-prx.token` — scanning for repo leaks. Running a repo-wide grep for token patterns and AWS creds.
nina: I've drafted a short customer message: "We detected anomalous authentication activity affecting a small number of inference requests between 14:20-14:28 UTC. We contained the activity, rotated service credentials, and are investigating whether any customer content was exposed. We will update within 4 hours." Sending to legal for sign-off.
ria: legal greenlight pending for wording and preservation note. Also want a confirmation that we did not rotate customer-facing credentials (only service token).
harper: confirming only the internal service token rotated. No customer API keys were touched.
alex: forensic notes: creating ips.txt of top offending IPs and will hand to netsec for blocklist and to infra for relation to ASN owners.
kyle: I pushed a temporary WAF rule and a CloudFront geo-limit for suspicious traffic patterns. Need to monitor for false positives.
nina: MediData contacted their security lead; we've opened an escalation channel and will provide redacted logs. Legal to advise on necessary disclosures.
ria: handoff: I'm handing incident lead to @alex for investigation & RCA. I'll remain on customer & legal coordination for next 6 hours. Alex you good?
alex: take it. Will produce initial RCA outline and a followup in 24h.
ria: summary timeline (for handoff message):
- 14:20:56 UTC: alert created for auth spike
- 14:22:00 UTC: security & oncall paged
- 14:24:10 UTC: runtime throttle + denylist applied
- 14:30:05 UTC: canary token deployed
- 14:33:59 UTC: old token revoked
- 14:35:12 UTC: prefix cache disabled and purge scheduled
- 14:40:00 UTC: customer comm draft sent to legal

ria: next action items (owners):
- alex: lead RCA, collect timeline + evidence (due 48h)
- harper: verify rotation automation & rotate backup keys (due 12h)
- kyle: repo & artifact scan for leakage indicators (ongoing)
- nina: customer comms and regulated-customer outreach (immediate)
- ria: coordinate legal & compliance (ongoing)

ria: keep updates in this thread. if any new anomalous traffic appears, page sec-pager again. :thumbsup:
